issues.body: beads_export_records selects newest using raw string ordering and only scan_beads_export_stale later parses that single value. For example, an old valid record plus any record whose timestamp is `zzzz` yields newest=`zzzz`; export_age_days returns None, stale becomes false, and an old export is not flagged unless the independent missing-reference count also happens to exceed 25. Thus a malformed field poisons all valid timestamp evidence instead of being skipped, despite the parser's documented tolerance and the report's `unparsable` wording.
issues.fix_hint: Parse each candidate timestamp while iterating, ignore invalid candidates, and compare normalized timezone-aware datetimes (retaining a canonical string for reporting). Add a test with an old valid timestamp and a lexicographically larger malformed timestamp, with no missing references, asserting that the stale finding still fires. This also avoids incorrect ordering if valid ISO-8601 timestamps use different UTC offsets.
issues.title: One malformed timestamp can suppress stale-export detection

verdict.summary: The new scanner is well scoped and its tests cover the normal age and missing-reference paths, but malformed timestamp handling can silently disable the age signal. The implementation chooses the lexicographically greatest raw timestamp before validating it; one malformed but lexicographically high field can therefore eclipse every valid timestamp, make export_age_days return null, and prevent a genuinely stale export from being reported when the missing-reference threshold is not exceeded. This contradicts the stated malformed-data tolerance and needs a focused regression test.
